answer_1.quote: Conditioned response generation has been extensively explored... and pre-training on unlabeled text or dialogue data does not help much.

answer_2.quote: Automatic Metrics We choose some widely used metrics in the literature : BLEU (Papineni et al., 2002) with n=1,2,3; ROUGE-L -longest common subsequence based statistics; CIDEr (Vedantam et al., 2015) utilizing TF-IDF weighting for each n-gram; and Distinct (Li et al., 2016a) indicating the proportion of unique n-grams (n=1,2) in the entire set of generated responses to evaluate response diversity.

answer_4.quote: Furthermore, we conduct manual evaluation on the best models according to the automatic metrics. We ask human evaluators to rate a response in {0, 1, 2}.
answer_4.guideline: A score of 0 means that the response might have flaw in fluency and logic or be incoherent; 1 represents a coherent but generic response; 2 represents a coherent and informative response. For condition consistency: 0 means inconsistent to the condition, 1 means somehow related, 2 means consistent. Flaws in fluency or logic result in a score of 0.
